content: The Two Generals Problem shows that two independent systems can never be 100% certain a cross-network operation was jointly committed when messages can be lost. Modern distributed architectures accept this and design for eventual consistency + idempotency + reconciliation rather than attempting synchronous 2PC across service/database boundaries -- the correct posture is 'assume the message might be duplicated or lost, make convergence and detection cheap' rather than 'prevent the uncertainty.'
